findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the `logging.getLogger(...)` call inside `assert_gated` from `"rebar.llm.config"` to `"rebar.llm.gate_context"` (or `__name__`) when the function is moved to `gate_context.py`, and note this in the Scope section.
evidence: config.py:230: `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config").warning(...)`
Plan lists `assert_gated` (`:216-240`) as part of the block being moved to gate_context.py
ABSENCE: no mention of updating the hardcoded logger name in either the Scope or Testing sections
findings.finding: The `assert_gated` function hardcodes `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config")` at config.py:230. After the function moves to `gate_context.py`, this logger identity becomes stale: any REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED override warning will be attributed to `rebar.llm.config` in logs even though the code runs from `rebar.llm.gate_context`. The plan does not mention updating this logger name.
scenarios: An operator sets REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED=1; the logged warning names 'rebar.llm.config' as source module instead of 'rebar.llm.gate_context', misleading anyone filtering or routing logs by logger name.
findings.suggested_fix: In the new `gate_context.py`, replace `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config")` with `logging.getLogger(__name__)` so the logger identity tracks the actual module automatically.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC2 and AC3: either narrow AC3 to 'ZERO edits to any existing *consumer* test file' (explicitly exempting the seam-guard test), or add a parenthetical in AC3 acknowledging the one deliberate guard-tightening edit required by AC2.
evidence: AC2: 'the seam guard for llm/config.py is TIGHTENED ... in tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py'
AC3: 'the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file'
Testing section: 'The relocation must require ZERO test edits. A required edit means the cut is wrong.'
findings.finding: AC line 2 explicitly requires editing an existing test file (`tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py` — tightening the LOC guard), while AC line 3 and the Testing section both state 'ZERO edits to any existing test file.' This is a direct cross-section contradiction: the implementer cannot simultaneously make zero edits to existing tests AND tighten the guard in that file.
findings.location: AC lines 2 and 3; Testing section ('The relocation must require ZERO test edits. A required edit means the cut is wrong.')
scenarios: An implementer reads AC3 and Testing section literally and does not edit the guard test, violating AC2.
An implementer edits the guard test to satisfy AC2, then AC3 as written is false — the plan's own stated pass criterion is violated.
A reviewer uses AC3 to reject a PR that correctly tightened the guard per AC2.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC3 to: 'the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file *other than the single LOC-guard tightening required by AC2*' — or equivalently, add '(the seam-guard edit in AC2 is the sole exception)' to AC3.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Scope item requiring an amendment to ADR 0056 §Decision 5 (or a new superseding ADR section) that records why the table approach was rejected and what was done instead, so the decision corpus stays truthful after this change ships.
evidence: The plan explicitly states ADR 0056's Decision 5 prescription 'does NOT hold' and spends ~10 paragraphs refuting it, but the Scope section lists no ADR update.
A future reader of ADR 0056 will see a recommendation (declarative field table) that the codebase has silently rejected, with the counter-reasoning living only in a closed ticket.
T5e criterion: 'A novel architectural decision is captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.'
findings.finding: ADR 0056 §Decision 5 is overridden by this plan but the ADR itself is not amended, leaving the repo's authoritative decision record with stale/contradictory guidance that will mislead future readers sizing up config.py.
findings.location: Approach section: 'ADR 0056 §Decision 5 pre-diagnosed this file and its prescription does NOT hold.'
scenarios: A future engineer reads ADR 0056 §Decision 5, attempts to implement the table approach, and breaks the env-var drift gate — exactly the failure mode the plan warns about but leaves undocumented in the ADR corpus.
A reviewer auditing ADR compliance flags the codebase as non-conformant with ADR 0056, triggering unnecessary remediation work.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: 'docs/adrs/0056-*.md — amend §Decision 5 to note that the declarative-field-table prescription was evaluated and rejected for config.py due to the AST-literal constraint in gen_env_registry.py; record the gate_context extraction as the adopted alternative and the two durable follow-ups (scanner extension, domain-split) as open items.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a guard test (alongside the LOC guard in `tests/unit/`) that AST-walks `src/` and asserts no file imports the moved names from `rebar.llm.gate_context` directly, matching the existing pattern of structural guard tests in the repo.
evidence: AC line 4 is a point-in-time check with no mechanism to prevent regression.
The plan explicitly warns: 'Repointing a consumer while a test patches rebar.llm.config.<name> is the silent-break mode ADR 0056 warns about.'
The plan adds a LOC headroom guard test but no import-path guard test.
findings.finding: The contract that no src/ module may import moved names directly from gate_context (AC line 4) is asserted as a one-time check but no guard test enforces it going forward, so a future developer can silently break monkeypatch targets by adding a direct import.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 4: 'no module under src/ imports the moved names from gate_context'
scenarios: A developer adding a new consumer of `current_code_root` writes `from rebar.llm.gate_context import current_code_root` (the obvious import), silently making any existing monkeypatch of `rebar.llm.config.current_code_root` a no-op and causing flaky test failures rather than loud collection errors.
findings.suggested_fix: In `tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py` (or a new peer file), add a test that walks `src/rebar/**/*.py` with `ast` and asserts that no `ImportFrom` node has `module == 'rebar.llm.gate_context'` and any of the moved names in its `names` list.
